title: Why Sudden Windfalls Vanish Faster Than Hard-Earned Savings
alt_title_1: Thaler & Johnson's 1990 Study on the House Money Effect
alt_title_2: The 30-Day Cooling Rule That Saves Bonuses and Tax Refunds
description_hook: In 1990, Nobel laureate Richard Thaler and economist Eric Johnson proved in Management Science that unexpected gains trigger reckless risk-taking known as the House Money Effect. Here is the 30-day rule that protects windfalls.

scenes.headline: Why Bonus Dollars Burn Twice as Fast
scenes.stat_label: FUNGIBLE CASH TREATED LIKE CASINO CHIPS
bullets: Every dollar has identical purchasing and compounding power
Yet sudden windfalls get spent or gambled away fast
scenes.narration: A thousand-dollar tax refund buys the exact same groceries as a thousand-dollar paycheck, yet people spend sudden windfalls far more recklessly.

scenes.headline: Thaler & Johnson's 1990 House Money Study
scenes.stat_label: GAMBLE RATE AFTER A WINDFALL VS BASELINE
bullets: 44% accepted a coin-flip gamble using baseline funds
77% gambled right after receiving an unexpected $30 gain
scenes.narration: In 1990, economists Richard Thaler and Eric Johnson proved the House Money Effect in Management Science. After receiving an unexpected thirty-dollar gain, seventy-seven percent of subjects took a coin-flip gamble versus forty-four percent normally.
scenes.source: Thaler & Johnson, 'Gambling with the House Money', Management Science (1990)

scenes.headline: Mental Accounting Numbs Normal Caution
scenes.left_body: Bonus or lucky trade -> rushed into speculative bets & upgrades
scenes.right_body: Merged into net worth -> guarded with strict sober discipline
scenes.narration: Mental accounting tags bonuses, inheritances, and lucky market gains as temporary casino chips, numbing normal loss aversion until the windfall evaporates.

scenes.headline: Enforce a 30-Day Treasury Cooling Lock
scenes.stat_label: COOLING PERIOD CONVERTS CHIPS TO CAPITAL
scenes.stat_subtext: 30 days untouched in T-bills -> brain reclassifies cash as savings
scenes.narration: Erase the casino label with a Thirty-Day Treasury Lock: park every unexpected payout in a quiet reserve account for one full month before touching a cent.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin behavioral rule inspired by Thaler & Johnson (1990)

scenes.headline: Let Windfalls Age Into Permanent Principal
scenes.stat_label: PAUSE IMPULSES SO SURPLUS CASH COMPOUNDS
bullets: Wait 30 days before allocating any bonus, refund, or payout
Spend at most 10% guilt-free and compound the remaining 90%
scenes.narration: Give sudden cash thirty calm days to feel like hard-earned principal so your windfalls actually compound.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
